patch:
diff --git a/solution.py b/solution.py
index b31bb56..edfcb5e 100644
--- a/solution.py
+++ b/solution.py
@@ -5,4 +5,16 @@ def word_wrap(text, width):
 
     e.g. word_wrap("the quick brown fox", 9) -> "the quick\nbrown fox".
     """
-    raise NotImplementedError
+    words = text.split()
+    if not words:
+        return ""
+    lines = []
+    current = words[0]
+    for word in words[1:]:
+        if len(current) + 1 + len(word) <= width:
+            current += " " + word
+        else:
+            lines.append(current)
+            current = word
+    lines.append(current)
+    return "\n".join(lines)
prompt: Implement `word_wrap(text, width)` in solution.py. It greedily wraps text into lines no longer than `width` characters, breaking only between words — for example word_wrap("the quick brown fox", 9) gives "the quick\nbrown fox". A word that's longer than `width` still goes on its own line (never split mid-word). Words are separated by whitespace and lines are joined with newlines. It should handle whatever whitespace the input has. The existing test shows the basic case.
title: Implement `word_wrap(text, width)` in solution.py
